commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 (PR #1300): removes hard-coded exemplar entry_is_line_a..e derived rules (proof atoms citing other chapters' HTS lines) from every generated chapter and makes them caller inputs; summary claims runtime semantics unchanged — unsure, part of the same decoupling repair.
description: The identifiers entry_is_line_a, entry_is_line_b, entry_is_line_c, entry_is_line_d, and entry_is_line_e are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: Chapter 74's authority-membership predicates were encoded as identity with five exemplar HTS lines from other chapters (72, 76, 95, 22, 85), so the section 301, section 232, section 201 and reciprocal-exclusion components were zero for every chapter 74 copper entry regardless of what the cited Chapter 99 notes cover.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 72: identical two hunks (summary rewrite + deletion of entry_is_line_a..e with their foreign-chapter proof atoms); normalized diff against index 72 differs only in blob hashes, chapter prefix, redundant-parenthesis count and the from/effective_from key spelling. None of the five exemplar lines is a chapter 74 line. Same doubt as index 72 about the retained 'runtime semantics are unchanged' boilerplate and the multi-commit repair sequence.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as bookkeeping or as a pure architectural decoupling and could not: the diff deletes five derived rules whose formulas were literal identity tests against HTS lines in other chapters (7202.11.10.00, 7601.10.30.00, 9506.62.40.40, 2203.00.00.30, 8541.42.00.10), each carrying proof atoms citing those other chapters' provisions, inside a chapter 74 copper module whose base rates come from ch74_general_rate[hts_line], so every one of them was statically false for any entry this module can price. Those flags are the sole gates on china_section_301_component_rate (all five terms), section_201_component_rate, section_232_aluminum_component_rate, and the annex/metals exclusion in section_122_component_rate, so chapter 74's authority stack was a constant fixed by other chapters' line identities rather than by the chapter 99 notes the module cites. Resolving the module's own cited provision us/statute/hts/9903.01.33 through the pinned release returns "articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum; ... semi-finished copper; and intensive copper derivative products" — copper is named in the cited text, yet the copper chapter's metals-exclusion predicate was `entry_is_line_b` (an aluminum wire line), which is exactly a formula grounded on the wrong provision. The fix removes those ungrounded predicates and makes the identifiers caller inputs "supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification," i.e. re-grounding, which is the untraceable_branch pattern and not a scope enhancement the module never claimed.
triage.verifier_notes:
Evidence trail: diff /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maxghenis-TheAxiomFoundation-axiom-encode--claude-worktrees-zealous-heyrovsky-31a96b/86103d8f-b97f-4559-a96c-7e79bdbe616d/scratchpad/diffs/us/2a6bdb01de/073.diff (124 lines: summary paragraph + removal of the five derived rules, nothing else); pre/post of us/policies/cbp/us-tariff-schedule/generated/ch74/ch74.yaml at 956a5474 and 2a6bdb01de.

Refutations I tested and rejected: (1) "mechanical" — the module summary's boilerplate "Values, dates, dtypes, proof atoms, and runtime semantics are unchanged" is contradicted by the diff, which deletes five derived outputs with formulas and proof atoms and moves them to the implicit caller-input surface; PR #1300 counts this as "-500 removed exemplar-flag outputs" across 100 chapters and its ledger ceiling moves 15770 -> 15470, so inputs and outputs changed. (2) "not_a_defect / new coverage" — the pre-state disagreed with a provision already in this module's own source_verification set (9903.01.33 names semi-finished copper), so the old text was wrong, not merely narrower. (3) "not_a_rule_module" — it is module.kind: composition, but it is a format: rulespec/v1 file with rules and formulas in a rulespec-us jurisdiction repo, not a compose spec/registry/ledger.

Closest alternative kind is wrong_entity_or_scope (a chapter 74 predicate keyed to chapter 72/76/95/22/85 line identities), but untraceable_branch explicitly covers formulas grounded on the wrong provision and is the better fit for a fix that deletes the ungrounded predicates.

Two caveats for the reviewer. (a) Direction is not uniform: for section 301 / 201 / 232-aluminum the flags being false zeroed the components, while for section_122 the false flags meant the annex and metals exclusions never fired, so the reciprocal component over-applied to copper; the candidate quote's phrase "reciprocal-exclusion components were zero" is accurate only in the sense that the exclusion predicate was false. (b) This commit is one half of PR #1300's repair — it removes the exemplar derivations while leaving the identifier names in the formulas; the sibling work in the same PR re-gates components on membership-semantic inputs ("never again zeroed by China-list or aluminum membership (the witness's exemplar coupling, which round-2 evaluation showed unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on 301-member lines for all origins)"). If the corpus policy is one defect per repair rather than per commit, this commit and the component-decoupling commit should be deduplicated into a single untraceable_branch defect rather than counted twice, and the same removal is replicated verbatim across all 100 generated chapter modules in this commit.
